headline: High: dexter’s broad networked autonomous execution can leak or misapply data when paired with a non-networked docs-only list that may be treated as trusted context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot inject directly. Profile B has autonomous execution and file/API surfaces, so if operators manually copy A’s content into B, prompt-style misuse is possible, but the bridge is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from agent_a into agent_b as instructions or scratchpad text, then injection risk exists.
IF agent_b parses copied text as authoritative guidance without provenance checks, then the risk materializes.
mitigations: Keep agent_a output read-only and separate from agent_b prompts.
Add a one-line provenance label before any copied text.
Review copied snippets before pasting into agent_b.
Use a dedicated scratch file for quotes only.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two workflows.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and has no egress, but agent B handles financial and market data, has broad network egress, and calls external APIs. If A’s outputs are fed into B’s workflow, B can transmit that context to third parties in default use, creating a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF agent_b receives any sensitive content from agent_a or the operator, then that content can flow to external APIs.
IF agent_b is run with its documented API integrations enabled, then outbound disclosure is possible.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive text from agent_a into agent_b prompts.
Disable unused external APIs in agent_b.
Use redacted summaries instead of raw content.
Rotate or scope API keys to least privilege.
requires-engineering: add DLP or outbound content filtering.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Agent B supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, so conflicts arise if multiple B instances share that directory or if A-derived artifacts are manually placed there. The overlap is real but not high because A itself is read-only.
conditions: IF two agent_b instances share the same .dexter/scratchpad/ directory, then write conflicts can occur.
IF operator-created artifacts from agent_a are stored in agent_b’s scratchpad, then file contention is possible.
mitigations: Give each agent_b instance a separate scratchpad path.
Avoid writing agent_a artifacts into agent_b working files.
Run only one agent_b instance per workspace.
Check for stale scratchpad files before launch.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a curated list, not an executing system, but its content can still be treated as authoritative reference material. Agent B’s autonomous execution and external API use mean that if A-derived recommendations are copied into B’s workflow without verification, B may act on them or propagate them downstream. The pathway exists in default operator workflows, though not by default in the profiles alone.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-derived text as factual input without verification, then cascading error can propagate.
IF agent_b takes actions based on unverified research outputs, then downstream mistakes can occur.
mitigations: Verify any A-derived claim before using it in B.
Require a second source for factual assertions.
Mark copied content as untrusted until checked.
Limit B to drafting, not acting, on imported claims.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B processes financial and market data and uses third-party APIs, while agent A is a docs-only open-source list with no data classes touched. The pair creates a compliance mismatch if regulated or sensitive financial data from B is exposed through external services or logs; A is not the compliance driver here, so it is cited mainly to show it does not add extra residency burden.
conditions: IF agent_b processes regulated financial data through external APIs, then retention/residency obligations apply.
IF logs or prompts retain financial data beyond policy, then compliance exposure exists.
mitigations: Confirm data-handling policy for financial data before use.
Avoid sending regulated data to external APIs.
Disable logging of prompts and outputs where possible.
Use synthetic or anonymized inputs for testing.
requires-engineering: implement retention and residency controls.
